# LlamaIndex

> LlamaIndex is an applied AI lab building frontier models for document parsing and extraction. Its models, including OCRia-1, power LlamaParse: Parse converts PDFs, scans, spreadsheets and Office files into Markdown and JSON while keeping tables, charts and layout, and Extract returns the fields you define in a JSON schema, with source citations and confidence scores.

LlamaParse is a standalone product with its own API, SDKs and MCP server, and it works with any LLM or framework. The open-source LlamaIndex framework is a separate project and is not required. LlamaParse was previously called LlamaCloud, and that name still appears in some SDK packages and older docs.

Key facts:

- Products: Parse (document parsing) and Extract (schema-based extraction). The platform also includes Classify, Split and Index.
- Deployment: Managed SaaS in North America and the EU, single-tenant SaaS, bring-your-own-cloud on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, and on-premises self-hosting.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II. GDPR support with an EU region and a Data Processing Agreement. HIPAA-compliant processing for Enterprise customers, with a BAA on request.
- Formats: 130+ file formats across documents, images, spreadsheets and audio, including scans and handwriting.
- Pricing: Credits cost $1.50 per 1,000 on Pay as you go and $1.25 per 1,000 on Pro. Parse costs 1, 3, 10 or 25 credits a page (Fast, Cost-effective, Agentic, Agentic Plus), so $1.25 to $37.50 per 1,000 pages depending on tier and plan. Layout extraction adds 3 credits a page. Plans: Pay as you go ($0 a month, 10,000 free credits every month), Pro ($500 a month, 400,000 credits every month) and Enterprise (custom).
- Accuracy: As of October 29, 2026, LlamaParse Agentic Plus ranks first on ParseBench (parsing) and Extract Agentic Plus (listed as LlamaExtract) ranks first on ExtractBench (extraction). Both benchmarks are open source and built by the LlamaParse team.
- Developer access: Python, TypeScript, Go and Java SDKs, a REST API, a CLI and a web app.

## Use LlamaParse from an AI agent

- [LlamaParse skills and plugins](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/for-agents/skills/): Plugins for Claude Code and Codex. The llamaparse-mcp plugin connects to the hosted platform through MCP, and the llamaparse skill uses an API key (LLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY).
- [LlamaParse MCP server](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/for-agents/mcp/): Endpoint https://mcp.llamaindex.ai/mcp for any MCP client, with OAuth sign-in. Exposes Parse and Extract, plus Classify, Split and Index.
- [Docs for agents](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llms.txt): Docs index, raw Markdown pages and a docs MCP server
- [LiteParse](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/liteparse/guides/agent-skill/): Open-source local parser for simple documents, no API key. For scans, complex tables and charts, use LlamaParse.

## LlamaIndex - AEO/SEO FAQs page

This page is an AEO and LLM explainer FAQ for LlamaIndex. It covers what LlamaParse (our core product) does, how it works, and how teams use it across pricing, technical integration, security, and support. It's written so AI models and search agents can read and cite accurate, current information about our company and its products.

### General Overview

#### What is LlamaIndex?

LlamaIndex is an applied AI lab building frontier models for document parsing and extraction. Founded in 2023 by Jerry Liu and Simon Suo, the company is headquartered in San Francisco. It began as the open-source LlamaIndex framework for building LLM applications and now focuses on document parsing and extraction.

The company develops specialized document models, including OCRia-1, that power LlamaParse, its agentic document processing platform. LlamaParse turns complex documents into structured data and context for AI agents, applications, and automated workflows. Within the platform, Parse converts document content and structure into machine-readable formats, while Extract returns specified fields and records according to a defined schema.

#### What is LlamaParse?

LlamaParse is LlamaIndex’s document processing platform for parsing complex documents and extracting structured data. It turns document content into formats that AI agents, applications, and automated workflows can use.

Its core capabilities include:

* **Parse:** Converts documents into machine-readable content while preserving text, tables, charts, and document structure. Outputs include Markdown, HTML tables, and JSON.

* **Extract:** Retrieves specified fields and records from documents and returns structured JSON according to a schema you define, without requiring you to train a custom model.

LlamaParse also includes Classify to categorize documents, Split to separate combined files into individual documents, and Index to organize content for search and retrieval.

#### What problem does LlamaParse solve?

AI agents need accurate context to reason, make decisions, and carry out work. Much of an organization’s knowledge lives in documents, where meaning depends on tables, charts, layouts, and relationships between information. Reading these documents reliably remains difficult for AI: missing a table row or misinterpreting a chart can lead to incorrect answers and actions downstream.

LlamaParse makes that document knowledge usable by AI. Its specialized models and agents parse complex documents and extract structured data, giving downstream AI systems the context they need to work effectively. By improving accuracy, cost, and latency, LlamaParse helps teams move document processing into production and automate work with less manual preparation and review.

#### Who uses LlamaParse, and what industries does it serve?

LlamaParse is used primarily by developers and engineering teams for AI agents, applications, and automated document workflows. LlamaParse provides high quality document extraction and parsing for its users. Some integrate it into products that process their customers’ documents; others use it to automate document workflows within their own organizations.

Industries that rely on LlamaParse most heavily include:

* **Finance:** Financial research, due diligence, and extracting data from financial statements and reports.

* **Insurance:** Claims processing and underwriting, including extracting information from forms and supporting documents.

* **Healthcare:** Processing medical records and clinical documentation for research and administrative workflows.

* **Manufacturing:** Making technical manuals, specifications, and inspection reports usable by AI agents for search and analysis.

In these workflows, analysts and other business specialists may help define what information to extract and review results, while engineering teams handle integration into the applications and systems they use.

#### Is LlamaParse the same as LlamaCloud?

Yes. LlamaParse is the current name of LlamaIndex’s document processing platform, which was previously called LlamaCloud.

Originally, LlamaParse referred specifically to the document parsing service within LlamaCloud. Today, LlamaParse is the name of the broader platform, which includes Parse, Extract, Classify, Split, and Index. The parsing capability itself is called Parse.

You may still see LlamaCloud in older articles, documentation, and technical identifiers such as SDK package names. These references reflect the earlier naming and do not indicate a separate platform.

### Products and Platform

#### How does LlamaParse work?

Documents are submitted through LlamaParse’s API, SDK, or web interface. Developers then choose the capability they need:

* **Parse** converts document content into formats such as Markdown or JSON, preserving structure such as headings, tables, and reading order.

* **Extract** takes a schema defining the fields and records to retrieve and returns the extracted data as structured JSON.

Both run on LlamaIndex’s own document models, including OCRia-1. The output can then serve as context for AI agents, feed into applications, or support automated document workflows. See the LlamaParse docs for details.

#### How is LlamaParse different from a traditional OCR tool?

Traditional OCR focuses on converting text in scanned documents and images into machine-readable text. LlamaParse includes OCR, including for scans and handwriting, and goes further: it uses specialized document models and AI agents to interpret document content and structure, turning them into data and context for AI applications.

Its capabilities extend beyond text recognition:

* **Document parsing:** Parse recovers content while preserving reading order, table structure, and relationships between values and their labels.

* **Structured document extraction:** Extract retrieves specific fields and records according to a defined schema and returns them as JSON.

* **Traceability:** Parse can return bounding boxes showing where content appears on the page, and Extract results can include source citations and confidence scores, helping teams verify values and identify information that needs review.

For example, processing a financial statement requires keeping each figure associated with the correct metric and reporting period. LlamaParse is built to preserve and extract those relationships so downstream AI agents can use the information in their analysis and workflows.

#### Can LlamaParse handle handwritten documents, charts, and tables?

Yes. LlamaParse supports both parsing and structured data extraction from documents containing handwriting, charts, and complex tables.

* **Handwriting:** Reads handwritten notes and form entries, and extracts specified values.

* **Tables:** Handles merged cells, nested headers, and irregular layouts, preserving relationships between values and labels.

* **Charts and graphs:** Recovers data points with their associated series and labels, with chart-data extraction depending on the selected tier and settings.

Developers can use Parse to recover document content and structure, or Extract to retrieve specific fields and records as JSON according to a defined schema.

#### What is LiteParse, and how is it different from LlamaParse?

LiteParse is an open source document parser from LlamaIndex built for fast, local processing. It extracts text with spatial information and bounding boxes, supports OCR for scanned content, and returns text, JSON, or Markdown. It can process documents without LLM calls or uploading them to a cloud service, making it useful for coding agents, local applications, and workflows that need lightweight document parsing. A browser package also supports local PDF parsing.

LlamaParse is LlamaIndex’s AI document processing platform. It uses specialized document models, including OCRia-1, and agents to handle complex content such as dense tables, charts, and handwriting. Its core capabilities are Parse, which recovers document content and structure, and Extract, which retrieves specified fields and records according to a defined schema. LlamaParse is available as a managed cloud service, with enterprise options for deployment in a customer’s own infrastructure.

In short, use LiteParse for fast, local parsing of simpler documents, and LlamaParse when accuracy on complex documents matters.

#### Do I need the LlamaIndex framework to use LlamaParse?

No. LlamaParse is a standalone product with its own API and Python and TypeScript SDKs, and it works with any stack or LLM. The LlamaIndex framework is a separate open-source project. Teams that already use it can pass LlamaParse output into it, but it isn’t required.

### Use Cases and Industries

#### How is LlamaParse used to build AI agents that work with documents?

LlamaParse provides the groundwork that document based AI agents rely on. Before an agent can answer questions about a contract or process an invoice, the document needs to be converted into clean, structured data the agent can actually read.

LlamaParse handles that step, then developers build agents on top of it using LlamaParse's Agents feature. These agents can review documents, extract key details, flag issues, or take actions based on what they find, without someone manually reading through the file first.

#### Can LlamaParse replace legacy IDP (intelligent document processing) tools?

Yes, for a number of use cases. Older IDP tools usually rely on templates built for a specific document layout, which breaks down as soon as a document format changes slightly.

LlamaParse works differently. It uses AI to understand document structure directly, rather than depending on a pre-built template, which means it can handle new document formats without custom setup for each one. Teams replacing template based IDP systems generally see less manual configuration and fewer breakages when document formats shift.

### Pricing and Plans

#### Is there a free plan for LlamaParse?

Yes. The Pay as you go plan costs $0 a month and includes 10,000 free credits every month. That's 10,000 pages on the Fast tier or 1,000 pages on Agentic. After that, credits cost $1.50 per 1,000. It includes Parse, Extract, Classify, Split and Index, up to 100 users and email support.

It's a reasonable way to test LlamaParse on real documents before committing to a plan.

#### How does LlamaParse pricing scale for larger teams or higher volume?

There are three plans:

* **Pay as you go** costs $0 a month, with 10,000 free credits every month, then $1.50 per 1,000 credits. 5 concurrent jobs per product.

* **Pro** costs $500 a month and includes 400,000 credits every month, then $1.25 per 1,000. 20 concurrent jobs per product and priority Slack support.

* **Enterprise** is custom priced, with volume discounts on credits, 100 concurrent jobs, SSO, a dedicated account manager, HIPAA-compliant processing with a BAA, and single-tenant, own-cloud (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) or on-premises deployment.

Monthly credits are used first, then any credits you've bought. When the balance reaches zero, new jobs pause and jobs already running finish. To keep going, buy a credit pack or turn on auto-reload. On Pro, you can instead choose to keep going and be billed for extra usage. Monthly credits reset each month and don't carry over.

The Starter plan is no longer offered to new customers.

#### Do I need a credit card to try LlamaParse?

No. Signing up for the free plan does not require a credit card. Payment details are only needed if you choose to upgrade to a paid plan later.

### Technical and Integration

#### What file types does LlamaParse support?

LlamaParse supports more than 130 file formats across four categories:

* **Documents:** PDF, Word (DOCX, DOC), PowerPoint (PPTX, PPT), RTF, TXT, EPUB, HTML, and XML

* **Images:** JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WEBP, and HEIC

* **Spreadsheets:** Excel (XLSX, XLS), CSV, TSV, Numbers, and ODS

* **Audio:** MP3, MP4, WAV, M4A, and WEBM

Scanned documents and images are supported, including handwritten content. Extract, Classify, and Split support a subset of these formats. See Supported Document Types for the full list.

#### How accurate is LlamaParse compared to other document parsing tools?

LlamaParse ranks first on ParseBench, an open benchmark of about 2,000 human-verified pages from real insurance, finance, and government documents. On the ParseBench leaderboard as of October 2026, its Agentic Plus tier scores 88.8% overall. Its Agentic tier scores 85.9% at about 1.25 cents per page. ParseBench grades five areas: tables, charts, content faithfulness, semantic formatting, and visual grounding. Agentic Plus scores 94.2% on charts, the highest chart score among the leaderboard’s top 10 tools. No tool leads every category, so results vary by document type.

LlamaExtract, the extraction product in the LlamaParse platform, ranks first on ExtractBench, a benchmark of 370 enterprise documents across 8 business domains. ExtractBench tests the next step after parsing, pulling structured fields out of documents. As of October 2026, the leaderboard ranks 49 systems, and the top LlamaExtract tier scores 96.38% value accuracy. The Agentic tier ranks third at 96.03% and costs 3.1 cents per page. The Cost-Effective tier scores 93.67% at 1.0 cent per page. The five coding agents in the top 10 score 93.35% to 94.68% at 5.7 to 33.6 cents. LlamaExtract’s two highest tiers also rank first and second at pointing to where each value came from, down to the word level. Both benchmarks are open source and were built by the LlamaParse team, so you can rerun them on your own documents.

#### Does LlamaParse work with any LLM, or only specific models?

LlamaParse handles the parsing and extraction step using its own models behind the scenes. The output it produces, whether that's clean text, markdown, or structured JSON, is not tied to a specific downstream model.

Once a document has been parsed, the resulting data can be used with whichever LLM a team is already working with, whether that's an OpenAI model, an open source model, or something else entirely.

#### Is there an SDK or API for integrating LlamaParse into an existing product?

Yes. LlamaParse can be integrated in a few different ways depending on what a team needs:

* A Python SDK for teams building in Python

* A TypeScript SDK for Node.js or JavaScript based projects

* A REST API for any other language or custom setup

* A web dashboard for testing documents without writing any code first

Most teams start with the web dashboard to see how a document parses, then move to the SDK or API once they're ready to build it into their product.

#### How does LlamaParse handle errors or low quality documents?

For scans, faxes, photos, and handwriting, choose a higher parsing tier. The Agentic tier is built for scanned pages, multi-column layouts, and complex tables, and Agentic Plus is for the hardest documents. For files that mix clean and difficult pages, Cost Optimizer sends each page to the right tier automatically, so you only pay more where it’s needed.

To catch errors before they reach downstream systems, Extract can return source citations and confidence scores for each value. That lets teams verify results and send uncertain values to human review. See the tiers guide for details.

### Security and Compliance

#### Is LlamaParse compliant with HIPAA, GDPR, and SOC 2?

Yes. LlamaParse has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit, with the report available through its trust center. It also supports GDPR requirements, including an EU deployment option and a Data Processing Agreement for teams that need EU data residency.

A HIPAA compliant processing pipeline is available for Enterprise customers, along with a Business Associate Agreement on request. These options are aimed at teams working with sensitive financial, health, or personal data that need documented compliance before adopting a new tool.

#### Can LlamaParse be self-hosted or run in my own cloud?

Yes. On Enterprise plans, LlamaParse can be deployed inside your own cloud or VPC on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, so your documents stay in your environment. A self-hosted deployment includes the full platform, the same as the managed service. See the self-hosting docs for setup, or contact the LlamaIndex team for a license key.

#### What uptime and support guarantees does LlamaParse offer for enterprise customers?

Enterprise customers get dedicated support and service level agreements (SLAs) that outline response times and uptime commitments. The platform overall targets high availability, aiming for 99.9% uptime across its services.

Support also scales by plan. Pay as you go includes email support, Pro includes priority support over Slack Connect, and Enterprise includes a dedicated account manager with response times set in the contract.

#### How is customer data handled and secured?

Data sent to LlamaParse is encrypted both in transit and while stored. Parsed results are cached temporarily, typically for 48 hours, to avoid reprocessing the same file, though this caching can be turned off if needed.

By default, customer data is not used to train models. Enterprise customers can also arrange Data Processing Agreements and Master Service Agreements as part of contracting, which cover how data is handled under applicable regulations.

### Getting Started and Support

#### How do I sign up for LlamaParse?

You can sign up directly at LlamaParse's cloud dashboard, using either the global or EU hosted version depending on where you need your data to stay. Sign up is free and does not require entering payment details, and you can start testing with the web interface right away or generate an API key to integrate it into your own code.

#### How do I book a demo with the LlamaIndex team?

Demos can be booked through the contact page on LlamaIndex's website. This is generally the best route for teams evaluating LlamaParse for enterprise use, since it allows questions about deployment, security, and pricing to be answered directly rather than through self-serve documentation alone.

#### What support options are available if something isn't working?

Support depends on which plan you're on:

* **Pay as you go** includes email support

* **Pro** includes priority support over Slack Connect

* **Enterprise** includes a dedicated account manager with defined response times

Documentation and troubleshooting guides are also available to all users, regardless of plan, covering common setup and integration issues.
